rounds.text: Disa India Ltd trades at a trailing price-to-earnings multiple of 31.1x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 5.83x [E2] on a market capitalization of ₹ 1,760 Cr [E3], which leaves the stock sitting at a notable 39% of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. While the bulls point to a discounted cash flow model suggesting intrinsic value of Rs 15,125 per share [E46], the fundamental bear-side screening reason explicitly flags that the stock trades below DCF value [E72]. Furthermore, the company's EV/EBITDA of 17.87x trades at a sharp premium against the sector benchmark of 12.62x [E11], exposing investors to multiple contraction risk if growth slows down. Conceded: the company boasts an ROA of 17.57% against a sector benchmark of 4.59% [E8], and a reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies 14.9% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case assumption [E48].
